title: AI-Powered Diabetic Retinopathy scanning Platform
subtitle: Detailed project presentation based on the implemented full-stack application in this repository.
bullets: Project type: multi-role healthcare web platform for diabetic retinopathy scanning and patient follow-up.
Core users: patients, doctors, diagnostic centers, technicians, and a super-admin reviewer.
Main value: connect retinal scan intake, AI-based grading, clinical review, reporting, appointments, and patient education in one system.
notes: Use this as the opening slide. Introduce the product as a complete workflow platform rather than only an AI model demo.

title: What The Project Delivers
bullets: A React 19 + Vite frontend with role-based dashboards and protected navigation.
A Node.js + Express backend with JWT auth, Google login, MongoDB persistence, and Cloudinary uploads.
A Python ResNet50 inference pipeline for retinal image classification integrated through the backend.
A Groq Llama 3.3 powered assistant and AI-generated clinical report summaries.
Operational features beyond AI: profile setup, appointments, notifications, reporting, and admin verification.
notes: Frame the platform as a product ecosystem. It is not just image classification; it includes user management and clinical operations.

title: Why This System Is Needed
bullets: Diabetic retinopathy scanning can be delayed when retinal scans must wait for manual review.
Hospitals and diagnostic centers often use fragmented tools for patient records, scan uploads, and specialist communication.
Patients need understandable results, appointment scheduling, and follow-up guidance after scans are reviewed.
Clinical systems also need role separation and verification before sensitive patient data becomes accessible.
notes: Connect the medical problem with the software architecture problem: delay, fragmentation, and security.

title: Project Goals And Stakeholders
bullets: Patients: register, complete profile, view reports, monitor analytics, chat with the diabetes assistant, and book appointments.
Doctors: maintain profile, review scan history, analyze cases, manage appointments, and receive notifications.
Diagnostic centers: create and manage patient records, upload scans, track reports, and refer cases for review.
Admin: verify doctor and diagnosis center registrations before they can access the system.
System goal: create a safe, traceable, end-to-end scanning workflow with AI support.
notes: Point out that stakeholder separation is reflected both in frontend routes and backend authorization rules.

title: High-Level System Architecture
bullets: Frontend SPA: React application served by Vite in development and by Express in production.
Backend API: Express server exposes auth, patient, doctor, scan, notification, center, chat, and appointment endpoints.
Database: MongoDB stores users, profiles, scans, appointments, notifications, and chat history.
Media storage: Cloudinary handles uploaded profile photos and retinal scans.
AI pipeline: backend launches Python inference for ResNet50 classification and calls Groq for summary generation.
notes: Mention that the server starts even if MongoDB is not ready, then responds with friendly 503 messages until connected.

title: Frontend Architecture And User Experience
bullets: Main stack: React 19, React Router 7, Tailwind CSS 4, Framer Motion, Lucide icons, Recharts, and jsPDF.
Core routing covers landing, login, registration, forgot password, profile setup, dashboards, reports, analytics, AI assistant, and appointments.
Context providers manage authentication, theme selection, language selection, and chat state.
Role protection is enforced through `PrivateRoute` and `RoleRoute` components.
UI includes multilingual support, profile-completion utilities, toasts, alerts modals, and settings/preferences flows.
notes: You can mention that the open file `DoctorRegistration.jsx` is part of the onboarding flow for doctor-specific profile capture.

title: Backend Modules And API Design
bullets: Server modules are split into controllers, routes, models, middleware, services, tests, and utility generators.
Routes include `/auth`, `/patients`, `/doctors`, `/scans`, `/notifications`, `/diagnosis-centers`, `/appointments`, and `/chat`.
Middleware includes JWT protection, role-based authorization, Cloudinary upload configuration, and CORS allowlist generation.
The server includes API 404 handling, a global error handler, static asset serving, and a database connection retry loop.
Production mode serves the frontend build directly from the backend process.
notes: This slide is useful to explain maintainability: the project follows a recognizable layered Express structure.

title: Core Database Models
bullets: User model stores identity, role, verification state, password or Google ID, avatar, reset fields, and security questions.
Patient model stores demographics, diabetes-related profile details, risk level, patient ID, and diagnostic center link.
Doctor model stores specialization, experience, degrees, contact info, photo, bio, and license number.
Scan model stores patient reference, image URL, eye side, AI result, confidence, findings, report summary, referral status, and bilateral flag.
Additional models cover diagnosis centers, appointments, notifications, and persistent chat history.
notes: Highlight that the app uses Mongoose references between User and role-specific profile documents.

title: Authentication, Authorization, And Safety Controls
bullets: JWT-based login is used for authenticated API access, with frontend request interceptors attaching tokens automatically.
Google OAuth login is supported through the backend auth controller and the frontend Google login flow.
Doctor and diagnosis center accounts enter a `pending` verification state until approved by admin.
Security questions are required during profile setup and are used in password recovery flows.
Additional guardrails include password complexity validation, future-date DOB blocking, CORS allowlisting, and role-based route checks.
notes: This is one of the strongest slides for academic or clinical review because it shows the system considers governance, not only features.

title: Retinal Image Analysis Workflow
bullets: Uploaded scan images are stored and then analyzed through `backend/ai/resnet_predict.py`.
The Python script loads a ResNet50 model with five output classes: Mild NPDR, Moderate NPDR, No DR, Proliferate DR, and Severe NPDR.
Softmax probabilities are converted into practical risk levels: Low, Moderate, or High risk.
The backend stores prediction, confidence, findings, lesion proxy count, and generated insights on the scan record.
Groq Llama 3.3 then creates a structured clinical summary with impression, patient explanation, and recommendations.
notes: Make it clear that the CNN handles classification while the LLM handles explanation and summarization.

title: Patient Journey In The Application
bullets: Patient registers with email/password or Google, then completes profile setup and security questions.
Patient dashboard and analytics views expose profile progress, scan history, and risk trends.
Patient report screens provide access to reviewed scan outcomes and exported report content.
Appointments can be booked with doctors, with backend rules preventing same-slot and invalid-date bookings.
The AI assistant provides diabetes-focused Q&A with persistent conversation history stored in MongoDB.
notes: Emphasize that patient engagement continues after diagnosis through reports, appointments, and education.

title: Diagnosis Center And Technician Workflow
bullets: Diagnosis centers can maintain their profile, manage patient records, and upload retinal scans.
Scan creation supports eye-side tagging and bilateral grouping using generated scan IDs.
If a center uploads a scan, the backend broadcasts notifications to doctors for review.
Centers can inspect historical scans and reports, giving them continuity across multiple visits.
Profile-completion utilities encourage centers to supply address, contact, type, license, and branding details.
notes: This slide shows the system supports real operational intake, not only doctor-side review.

title: Doctor Workflow And Clinical Review
bullets: Doctors maintain a detailed profile including specialization, degrees, experience, contact details, and photo.
Doctor dashboards show scan queues, patient details, and prior scanning history.
Doctors can trigger AI analysis, inspect confidence and findings, and review the generated clinical summary.
Doctors manage patient appointments and can update appointment status to pending, confirmed, rejected, or completed.
Notifications keep doctors aware of new diagnostic requests and workflow events.
notes: If presenting live, explain that doctors remain in the loop for final review instead of handing decisions fully to AI.

title: Administrator Verification Portal
bullets: Admin login is supported through the auth flow and opens a dedicated admin dashboard.
Admin can inspect doctor and diagnosis center accounts by status: pending, verified, or rejected.
Verification is not cosmetic; login access for those roles is blocked until approval is granted.
The dashboard includes search, analytics cards, and segmented lists for account auditing.
This design reduces the risk of unverified clinical users gaining access to patient workflows.
notes: Explain that governance is built into both backend checks and frontend management screens.

title: Appointments, Notifications, And Chat
bullets: Appointments enforce business rules: future scheduling, one appointment per doctor per day, and no duplicate active bookings.
Notification records support report, system, security, and appointment events and can be read, cleared, or deleted.
Chat history is stored per user, so the AI assistant session persists between visits.
The assistant is intentionally constrained to diabetes-related topics for safer domain focus.
Speech recognition with silence detection allows hands-free message input on the frontend.
notes: This slide helps show product maturity: the app includes operational glue features that users actually need.

title: Validation, Testing, And Reliability Measures
bullets: Backend tests currently cover CORS configuration and patient password utility behavior using Node's built-in test runner.
Input validation exists for email format, password strength, DOB rules, message length, appointment constraints, and profile fields.
The backend includes friendly 503 responses when MongoDB is unavailable instead of crashing immediately.
Database connection retry logic and placeholder image fallback improve resilience in imperfect deployment conditions.
Profile-completion scoring utilities are implemented for doctor, patient, and diagnosis center flows.
notes: Be honest that testing exists but is still limited relative to the full feature set.

title: Environment And Deployment Model
bullets: Root `npm run dev` runs backend and frontend concurrently for local development.
Frontend defaults to `http://localhost:5001/api` during local dev unless `VITE_API_BASE_URL` is supplied.
Backend expects environment variables such as `MONGO_URI`, `JWT_SECRET`, Google client values, and `GROQ_API_KEY`.
Frontend contains Vercel configuration while the backend can serve the production frontend build directly.
Cloudinary and MongoDB Atlas are external dependencies for media persistence and application data.
notes: This is the implementation-grounded deployment story visible from the repository, not a hypothetical cloud design.

title: Strengths, Current Gaps, And Future Scope
bullets: Strengths: multi-role design, real AI integration, persistent data model, secure onboarding, and strong end-to-end workflow coverage.
Current gaps: limited automated test coverage, Python inference dependency management, and room for deeper audit logging and analytics.
Possible future work: model performance reporting, report approval workflows, stronger clinical explainability, calendar integration, and richer admin auditing.
The codebase already provides a strong foundation for scaling into a production-grade retinal scanning product.
notes: This slide is important for viva, demo, or investor-style presentation because it shows balanced judgment.

title: Project Conclusion
bullets: Retinal AI combines healthcare workflow design with AI-assisted retinal scanning in a single application.
The repository demonstrates full-stack implementation depth across UI, API, database, security, and AI integration.
It is suitable to present as both a software engineering project and a healthcare technology solution.
The generated presentation assets can now be used directly for classroom, demo day, or stakeholder presentation.
notes: Close by tying together technical depth and healthcare impact.
